docs: fix onStepStart event fields in generate-text reference (#24195)

## Background

The `onStepStart` entry in the `generateText` reference documents five
fields that are not part of `GenerateTextStepStartEvent` (`timeout`,
`headers`, `stopWhen`, `abortSignal`, `include`) and omits `callId`,
which is part of the event. Copying the documented fields produces
TypeScript errors. This was previously noted as future work in #21692.

## Summary

Updated the `GenerateTextStepStartEvent` parameter table to match the
source type: added `callId` and removed the five fields that belong to
`generateText` options, not to the event.

The five removed fields produce `TS2339` when destructured from the
event. The updated table matches the type exactly: 15 fields documented,
15 in `GenerateTextStepStartEvent`, no differences. `pnpm validate:docs`
and `pnpm run check` pass.

fix(harness-opencode): ensure OpenCode ignores repo-specific settings (#24415)

## Background

OpenCode loads `opencode.json[c]` and `.opencode/` config from the
session working directory and its parents, and that config takes
precedence over the policy the bridge sets.

## Summary

The bridge now starts OpenCode with `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1`,
so the bridge-provided config is the only source of policy.

Since that flag also turns off OpenCode's own `AGENTS.md` discovery, the
bridge passes `<workdir>/AGENTS.md` as an absolute `instructions` entry.
OpenCode renders it in the same place in the system prompt and re-reads
it every step, just like before.

- Only the working directory's `AGENTS.md` is loaded, no longer
`AGENTS.md` from parent directories, `CLAUDE.md`, or `CONTEXT.md`.
Skills in `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills` keep working;
`.opencode/skill(s)` in the repository no longer load.
- Relative entries in the host-provided `openCodeConfig.instructions`
are resolved against the working directory (they'd otherwise resolve
against OpenCode's global config directory).
- The bridge refuses to start if the working directory is or contains
the sandbox home directory or OpenCode's global config directory, since
OpenCode always loads config from those.

Version Packages (#24410)

This PR was opened by the [Changesets
release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When
you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will
be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release
yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will
be updated.


# Releases
## ai@7.0.162

### Patch Changes

- 857ca45: Restore server-defined tool metadata, dynamic status, and
title when validating tool approval continuations so approval policies
receive the same tool definition fields as new model calls.
- 4d6d830: Support a single telemetry operation for durable
`WorkflowAgent` runs, including the prompt, final output, steps, and
tools. Events recorded in the workflow are reported on completion or
suspension with their original timestamps. For OpenTelemetry, pass the
same `OpenTelemetryIdGenerator` instance as the tracer provider's
`idGenerator` and `sampler` and as `new OpenTelemetry({ durable })`.
This explicit bridge carries parent trace context and sampling across
steps, reports model spans live with provider requests nested beneath
them, and reconstructs the enclosing `invoke_agent` tree when the run
completes. Without the bridge, existing live per-model tracing is
preserved. Add typed experimental durable context hooks for telemetry
integrations; remove reliance on process-global ID-generator detection.

fix(provider-utils): require patched undici for CVE-2026-84961 (#24420)

## Background

VULN-14657 flags Undici 7.29.0 in `@ai-sdk/provider-utils` for
CVE-2026-84961 (GHSA-w293-vg96-wgc3). The advisory affects
`BalancedPool` with function-valued TLS/connection options; the SDK uses
`Agent`, so this change removes the affected dependency version without
claiming a demonstrated SDK exploit.

## Summary

Raise the published Undici dependency minimum from `^7.29.0` to
`^7.29.1`, select 7.29.1 for provider-utils in the lockfile, and add a
patch changeset. This is a package manifest change, so downstream
consumers receive the fixed minimum too.

Other dependency paths in the monorepo are outside this ticket's
provider-utils scope and can still select older Undici versions.

## End-to-End Verification

Exercised the built local provider-utils public
`fetchWithValidatedEndpoint` API against https://example.com using its
default Undici transport, before and after the dependency update. No
credentials are needed. Requires the repository's supported Node/pnpm
versions and outbound HTTPS access. No CVE exploit reproduction was
performed: the SDK uses `Agent`, which the advisory explicitly excludes.

Save this script outside the checkout as
`/private/tmp/vuln-14657-smoke.mjs`:

```js
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
const root = process.argv[2];
const require = createRequire(`${root}/packages/provider-utils/package.json`);
const { version } = require('undici/package.json');
const { fetchWithValidatedEndpoint } = await import(pathToFileURL(`${root}/packages/provider-utils/dist/index.js`));
const response = await fetchWithValidatedEndpoint({
  url: 'https://example.com/',
  abortSignal: AbortSignal.timeout(20000),
});
const body = await response.text();
console.log({ undici: version, status: response.status, exampleDomain: body.includes('Example Domain') });
```

From the relevant checkout root, run these commands before the change
and again after it:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm exec turbo build --filter=@ai-sdk/provider-utils...
node /private/tmp/vuln-14657-smoke.mjs "$PWD"
```

The script loads `dist/index.js` by absolute path and resolves Undici
relative to that checkout's provider-utils manifest, rather than using a
published SDK package.

Before: `{ undici: '7.29.0', status: 200, exampleDomain: true }`

After: `{ undici: '7.29.1', status: 200, exampleDomain: true }`

## Validation

- Frozen install and supply-chain policy checks passed.
- Provider-utils build passed (3 tasks).
- Provider-utils tests passed: 1,190 Node tests / 96 files and 1,172
Edge tests / 93 files.
- `pnpm type-check:full` passed.
- `pnpm check` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

No new tests were added for the dependency-only change; existing
transport coverage was rerun.

fix(harness-cursor): add missing write tool definition (#24411)

## Background

Latest Cursor CLI reports file writes with a `Write <path>` permission
title, but the adapter did not define that built-in. The path-only input
then matched multiple file tools, so the bridge emitted a dynamic
`acp_tool_call-*` name and AI SDK raised `AI_NoSuchToolError`.

## Summary

- Add Cursor's `Write` built-in using the observed `edit` kind,
path-only input, and native name `writeToolCall`.
- Add runtime and type-level coverage for the built-in definition.
- Keep Cursor installation on the official unpinned installer.

## Contributor Credit

N/A.

## End-to-End Verification

Prerequisites: set `CURSOR_API_KEY` and configure Cursor CLI for direct
model-provider routing. `examples/ai-functions` resolves both harness
packages through `workspace:*` dependencies.

Build the local packages and run the reproduction:

```sh
pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/harness-acp build
pnpm --filter @ai-sdk/harness-cursor build
./tools/run-harness-agent-examples.sh --example with-outside-workdir-reads --auth direct --harness cursor
```

Before the change, the write call was emitted as `acp_tool_call-*` and
produced `AI_NoSuchToolError`. After the change, the CLI call is
identified as `write` with `nativeToolName: "writeToolCall"`.

The write and read complete, but the example exits with `Expected a read
permission request` because no explicit read approval was emitted. That
expectation is separate from this fix.

## @ai-sdk/harness@1.0.172

### Patch Changes

- 8a20b57: feat(harness): defer sandbox setup, and optionally sandbox
creation, to first use for harnesses without a bootstrap recipe

For a harness adapter that declares no sandbox bootstrap recipe (such as
Pi), `HarnessAgent.createSession()` no longer runs the session's sandbox
setup (`onBootstrap` when its marker is missing, the session work
directory, and `onSession`) before the adapter starts. The setup runs on
the first file, exec or spawn operation on the sandbox, and a failed
setup is retried on the next one. Adapters with a recipe, such as Claude
Code and Codex, keep setting up the sandbox in `createSession()`.

`sandboxSession` also accepts a `HarnessAgentSandboxCreator`, `{
defaultWorkingDirectory, createSandboxSession }`, to defer creating the
sandbox itself. For an adapter without a recipe, `createSandboxSession`
runs on the first file, exec or spawn operation, so a session whose
turns never touch the sandbox never creates it. For any other adapter,
`createSession()` calls it right away.

## @ai-sdk/harness@1.0.172

### Patch Changes

- 8a20b57: feat(harness): defer sandbox setup, and optionally sandbox
creation, to first use for harnesses without a bootstrap recipe

For a harness adapter that declares no sandbox bootstrap recipe (such as
Pi), `HarnessAgent.createSession()` no longer runs the session's sandbox
setup (`onBootstrap` when its marker is missing, the session work
directory, and `onSession`) before the adapter starts. The setup runs on
the first file, exec or spawn operation on the sandbox, and a failed
setup is retried on the next one. Adapters with a recipe, such as Claude
Code and Codex, keep setting up the sandbox in `createSession()`.

`sandboxSession` also accepts a `HarnessAgentSandboxCreator`, `{
defaultWorkingDirectory, createSandboxSession }`, to defer creating the
sandbox itself. For an adapter without a recipe, `createSandboxSession`
runs on the first file, exec or spawn operation, so a session whose
turns never touch the sandbox never creates it. For any other adapter,
`createSession()` calls it right away.

fix(topaz): reject redirects when uploading input videos (#24388)

Topaz input-video uploads validate the initial response-supplied URL but
let native fetch follow redirects. Route the PUT through
`fetchWithValidatedEndpoint`, using the configured base URL as
`trustedOrigin`, so redirects are rejected and untrusted hosts use the
default DNS-pinned fetch. Preserve the video body, content type, abort
signal, user agent, and omission of API credentials.

Adds regression coverage for 307/308 rejection and cancellation,
custom-fetch request options, blocked private upload URLs, and
explicitly configured private origins. Includes a patch changeset.

Validation:
- Topaz tests: 90 passed in Node and 90 passed in Edge.
- Topaz type check and changed-file lint/format checks passed.
- Full workspace type check passed after generating Nuxt example types.
- New fetch-policy assertions fail against the original uploader.

Also applies to `release-v6.0`, addressed in a separate PR. v4/v5 do not
contain this uploader; the generated `changeset-release/main` branch
inherits the fix from `main`.

Companion PR: https://github.com/vercel/ai/pull/24389

docs: require end-to-end bug verification in PR descriptions (#24384)

## Background

The bug-fix instructions direct agents to put reproductions in
`examples/ai-functions`, which led to one-off debugging scripts being
committed. Bug fixes need end-to-end evidence before and after the
change, with the reproduction recorded in the PR body.

## Summary

- Require reproducing the failure end-to-end before changing production
code, then rerunning the same reproduction against the fix through the
affected public API and real provider or application flow where
applicable.
- Keep reproduction-only files outside the checkout. Put the complete
runnable source, setup and execution commands, prerequisites without
secrets, and observed before/after results in the template's
**End-to-End Verification** section.
- Build and use the relevant checkout's local packages for both runs.
Include a concrete stdin execution example so a temporary script
resolves workspace packages, and require showing that setup in the PR
body.
- Record verification limits and blocked runs explicitly; unit tests and
mocked requests do not replace end-to-end verification. Keep regression
tests and reusable examples in the repository.
- Align `AGENTS.md`, both AI function example skills, and the PR
template.

Validation: formatting passes for all four changed Markdown files, both
skills pass `quick_validate.py`, and `git diff --check` passes. Built
the packages with the documented filters and verified a temporary script
executed through stdin resolves `ai` and `@ai-sdk/openai` to this
checkout's `packages/*/dist/index.js` files. This changes documentation
only.

Claude Code `--model opus` review and follow-up found no blockers.
Incorporated its local-package resolution and template-scoping
suggestions, clarified that the rule applies to reproduction-only files
anywhere in the repository while allowing reusable examples for fixed
behavior, and moved temporary bug reproductions out of the skill's list
of examples to add.

- [x] All commits are signed (PRs with unsigned commits cannot be
merged)
- [ ] Tests have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [x] Documentation has been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] A _patch_ changeset for relevant packages has been added (for bug
fixes / features - run `pnpm changeset` in the project root)
- [x] I have reviewed this pull request (self-review)
